messages.body_plain:
Hi Filipe,

It's not a major issue with the IDs, as long as each individual polygon gets an ID, it's not too difficult to assign them afterwards, but if it can be coded, that would still be useful.. I have a number of multispectral orthomosaics, and a shapefile that I created in ArcMap, would it be possible to demonstrate how I could do this? I've included the download link here: https://1drv.ms/u/s!AmYm6I8Zg5lThEKO0i4QB6-h2xPt?e=6X93YY.

Perhaps you could help with a separate issue, I do seem to be getting errors, which I think are related to the coordinate system, which is UTM (projected). I wasn't getting these errors when I tried a separate dataset that had a geographic coordinate system. Do I need to convert the coordinate system to geographic before using FieldImageR?

Kind Regards,

Dan

Hi Filipe,

Thanks for getting back to me. Sorry, I should have been more specific: The first error I get is when I import both the shapefile and the orthomosaic:

"Warning message: In OGRSpatialRef(dsn, layer, morphFromESRI = morphFromESRI, dumpSRS = dumpSRS, :   Discarded datum Geocentric_Datum_of_Australia_1994 in Proj4 definition: +proj=utm +zone=56 +south +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs"

When I continue and try to run the fieldInfo function, I get an error saying:
Error in fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.5b.Indices[[c("NDVI", "NDRE", "RVI", "GNDVI", : fieldShape and mosaic must have the same projection CRS. Use fieldRotate() for both files.

This is strange, since when I open my orthomosaic and shapefile in ArcMap they are perfectly aligned with each other.. It seems like there is an issue with the spatial reference systems in my datasets. Is it necessary to rotate my shapefile and mosaic if they're already aligned when I import them?

The full code is here: Thanks very much for your help!

library(FIELDimageR)
library(raster)
library(rgdal)

setwd('R:/ISMAILUAV-A5263/Field trial 2021/UAV Flights')

shapefile <- readOGR("GIS/shapefile/shapefile.shp")

# Uploading multispectral mosaic:
EX1.5b <- stack("orthos/2021-06-22_P4M_ortho.tif")

EX1.5b.Indices <- fieldIndex(EX1.5b,Red=3,Green=2,Blue=1,RedEdge=4,NIR=5,
                             index = c("NDVI","NDRE", "RVI", "GNDVI", "TVI", "CVI", "EVI", "CIG", "CIRE", "DVI"))

EX1.5b.Info <http://EX1.5b.Info><- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.5b.Indices[[c("NDVI","NDRE",
                                                   "RVI", "GNDVI", "TVI", "CVI", "EVI", "CIG", "CIRE", "DVI")]],fieldShape = shapefile ,n.core = 3)

EX1.5b.Info <http://EX1.5b.Info>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Filipe,

It seems like the coordinate reference system was slightly different for my shapefile and mosaic:

crs(EX1.5b)
CRS arguments: +proj=utm +zone=56 +south +ellps=GRS80 +units=m +no_defs

crs(shapefile)
CRS arguments: +proj=utm +zone=56 +south +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs

I solved the issue by forcing the coordinate reference system for the shapefile and mosaic to be exactly the same...

crs(shapefile) <- "+proj=utm + zone=56 +south +ellps=GRS80 +units=m +no_defs"
crs(EX1.5b) <- "+proj=utm + zone=56 +south +ellps=GRS80 +units=m +no_defs"

This brings me to my next question: How would you recommend removing the soil from multispectral imagery? Should I use the recommended "HUE" index, or try something else such as NDVI?

Kind Regards,

Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Amplitude de índices
messages.subject_clean: Amplitude de índices
messages.body_plain:
Oi Igor,

Obrigado por entrar em contato. Como você mesmo descreveu os índices normalizados
devem variar de -1 a 1. Quando a formula dos índices não seguem linearidade
pode haver variações nos valores além desses limites.

Alguns dos seus índices que você perguntou não estão implementados como NGBDI,
VWRI, e EXG. Não sei dizer se eles têm alguma parte da equação que possui elevações
(^2) ou outros não linearidades. No entanto, os índices que você perguntou que fazem parte do pacote devem seguir a regra.

Você está coletando a média ou a soma por pot.?

As formulas do pacote seguem as descritas no tutorial https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6.

Obrigado,

Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

I am glad that you figured out the projection issue.

Removing or not the soil is related to your objectives. If you want to observe only the plants' reflection aspects per se or genetics performance I recommend removing the soil. However, if you are looking for information as a leaf area index, which is a proportion/relation to plants covering the soil, or traits related directly to canopy cover I will recommend keeping the soil to extract the data.

Is that make sense?

About the index to remove the soil, you need to try to find what index provides better plants and soil separation in the image. In general, "HUE" works great. However, I've seen some cases where NGRDI or BGI works better. Please, check the second part of this link for more information: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6.

All the best,
Filipe

messages.body_plain:
Hi EJ,

It's not working because you are using fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape@data.

@data is a dataset and not a shapefile. You only need to remove it from your code and use fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape

Here is the code that worked for me:

library(FIELDimageR)
library(raster)

EX1 <- stack("IMG_0046_merged.tiff")
EX1.Crop <- fieldCrop(mosaic = EX1)
EX1.BGI<- fieldMask(mosaic = EX1.Crop, Red = 1, Green = 2, Blue = 3,
                    index = "BGI", cropValue = 0.6, cropAbove = T)
EX1.Shape<-fieldShape(mosaic = EX1.BGI,ncols = 6, nrows = 8)

EX1.Indices <- fieldIndex(EX1.BGI$newMosaic,Red=1,Green=2,Blue=3,RedEdge=4, ###Indices####

                          index = c("GLI"))
EX1.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic = EX1.Indices$GLI,

                     fieldShape = EX1.Shape$fieldShape,

                     projection = F,
                     n.core = 3)

Please, let me know if it works.

All the best,
Filipe
